clue.text: Waste energy to operate fiddle

parts.note: scrap is waste material, rubbish
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone squanders effort on running a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a swindle, but here it is a violin; to scrape is to play one badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape a bow across strings is a dismissive way of saying someone plays the violin.

clue.text: Pretentious air actually existing among stars

parts.note: side is an old word for pretentious, superior manner
real means actually existing

explanation.surface: A celebrity's affectations are genuine among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to the stars, as in sidereal time measured against them.

clue.text: The rest live around university

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Everyone else lives near the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the remainder or rest of something.

clue.text: Feel anger towards being taken in by a frontman

indicators.note: being taken in means the anger word sits inside the other piece

parts.note: per means for each or by a, as in per annum
to resent is to feel bitterness towards

explanation.surface: A man resents being conned by a band's lead singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter fronts a broadcast, so is its frontman.

clue.text: Posh car following street buggy

indicators.note: following puts the car piece after the street piece in the answer

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car

explanation.surface: A luxury car drives behind a baby's pushchair down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A buggy and a pushchair for a small child are the same thing, a synonym.

clue.text: Admitting taking steps, knowing what one has in mind

definitions.text: knowing what one has in mind

parts.note: though can mean admitting that, conceding
treading is walking, taking steps

explanation.surface: Admitting you are taking steps shows you know your own mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought-reading is telepathy, perceiving what another person is thinking.

clue.text: Charity needs steer over footballers with money

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, puts the steer piece on top of the rest

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: A charity needs cattle, footballers and cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a large British charity fighting poverty, so an example of a charity.

clue.text: A politician in mostly crazy satire

indicators.note: in means the politician sits inside the crazy word
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: loony means crazy
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A lawmaker is caught up in a rather mad piece of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a mocking piece of writing, a satire.

clue.text: Anger about theologian's tricky question

indicators.note: about means the anger word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to rile is to anger
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A theologian's hard question provokes anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question, deliberately tricky.

clue.text: Mention Nick … here he comes!

parts.note: to talk of something is to mention it
Old Nick is a name for Satan

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a man called Nick just as he arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is used when someone appears just as they are being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is exclaimed when a person turns up while being spoken about.

clue.text: Outlaw posed scruffily keeping challenge to return

indicators.note: keeping means the scrambled letters hold the next piece inside them
scruffily suggests the letters of posed are messed up into a new order
to return means the word for challenge is read backwards

parts.note: to dare is to challenge

explanation.surface: A bandit poses untidily while holding out a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffily' gives DESPO and 'to return' gives ERAD; 'keeping' places the reversed challenge just before the final letter of the rearranged pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, and an outlaw is a fugitive criminal: near synonyms.

clue.text: Having celebrity, this person is caught in passing craze

indicators.note: is caught in means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
the setter refers to themselves, giving me

explanation.surface: A celebrity finds themselves part of a passing fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known, having celebrity, is the state of being renowned.

clue.text: Right-wing American somehow reckoned to ditch Obama at first

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of reckoned are rearranged in some way, minus what is ditched
at first selects the opening letter of Obama

explanation.surface: A conservative American calculates how to get rid of Obama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles RECKONED; 'to ditch' with 'at first' removes O, the first letter of Obama, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A redneck is a stereotyped rural white American, typically seen as politically right-wing.

clue.text: Cajun stew — one left pain in the mouth

parts.note: gumbo is a thick stew from Louisiana's Cajun cooking
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eating a Cajun stew is left with a sore mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboil is a painful abscess on the gum, so literally a pain in the mouth.

clue.text: A section downsized with skill

parts.note: dept is the shortened form of department, a section of an organisation

explanation.surface: One part of a company is skilfully cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adept is skilled, so the adjective describes a person acting with skill.

clue.text: Fine work of art is attractive

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate, a work of art

explanation.surface: A fine artwork is pleasing to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching describes someone or something charming and good-looking, a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Passes fish agreement

parts.note: hands means passes, as in hands over
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone passes over a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A handshake seals a deal, so it stands for an agreement.

clue.text: Protector of flock to collect old money keeping nothing

indicators.note: keeping means the outer pieces hold the next one inside

parts.note: to gather is to collect
O looks like zero, nothing
D was the old British penny

explanation.surface: A shepherd goes to collect old coins but keeps nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: D, for denarius, was the penny in Britain's pre-1971 currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatherd tends goats, looking after and protecting the flock.

clue.text: Protective footwear for work in garden after excesses

indicators.note: after puts the garden piece behind the excesses piece

parts.note: overs are surpluses or excesses, as in overs and unders
to hoe is to break up soil or weed in a garden

explanation.surface: Galoshes are needed for gardening after overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: An overshoe is a rubber or fabric covering worn over a shoe to protect it.

clue.text: Composer anticipates court decision

indicators.note: anticipates means comes before, putting the composer first

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer foresees the judgment in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a judgment reached, a decision.

clue.text: Pick from selection a choice snack

indicators.note: pick from tells us to take a run of letters out of the following words

explanation.surface: Choosing a nibble from an assortment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, often topped, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Talk going round Brazilian city in vehicle

indicators.note: going round means the talk word wraps the city

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city

explanation.surface: People talk while driving round Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, an old vehicle.

clue.text: A cheap reconditioned helicopter

indicators.note: reconditioned means rebuilt, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A cheap refurbished helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache is an American attack helicopter, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Means to dispose of dead mostly surrounded by massive monument

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning a corpse
amid means in the middle of, surrounded by

explanation.surface: A great tomb surrounds the dead and the methods for disposing of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids are huge stone tombs, the classic example of a massive monument.

clue.text: Gibson perhaps willing to get fruit

parts.note: Mel Gibson is the actor, giving the first name
on means willing, as in I'm on for it

explanation.surface: An actor called Gibson is keen to get some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family.

clue.text: Singing style let flow over listeners finally

indicators.note: over here means one piece covers another, holding it inside

parts.note: to decant is to pour liquid out gently

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of listeners

explanation.surface: A singer's manner flows over the audience at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives S, which 'over' sets inside DECANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a decorative melody sung above the main tune, a style of singing.

clue.text: Central heating ailing — one may get this

parts.note: CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating
ailing means ill

explanation.surface: With the central heating broken, someone falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole surface: with the heating ailing, one may catch this.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a cold or shivering feeling, something a person catches.

clue.text: Cause damage to London museum's Elizabeth the First of England

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
Liz is a short form of Elizabeth

indicators.note: the First of picks the initial letter of England

explanation.surface: A London museum's royal portrait of Elizabeth I is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the First' looks like a regnal number for Elizabeth, but it picks E from England.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalize is to wreck property deliberately, causing damage to it.

clue.text: Snare fish after net damaged

indicators.note: after places the fish piece behind the rearranged net
damaged suggests the letters of net are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Someone catches fish once their net is torn.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to catch in a mesh or trap, so it means to snare.

clue.text: Checked out old soldier's unruly youth

parts.note: vet is short for veteran, an old soldier
Ted is short for Teddy boy, a rebellious 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: An elderly veteran's wayward son is investigated.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet someone is to examine them carefully, so checked out is a synonym.
